name: greybox-blockout
about: The stand-in look of a generated game and the route its art takes: what the generator template holds, what stops its run, what the user has decided and what is still open. An agent hands the model the deliver steps and runs the confirm steps on what comes back.

status.enforced: held by the template, and a check stops the generator's run when it is broken
status.adopted: decided by the user; held by the template where it names a template value, else for the generator to follow; no check
status.open: the template holds a value the user has not chosen yet
status.proposed: evidence only; not in the template
status.rejected: tried or considered and turned down; do not reintroduce

grid.UNIT: 8 when the viewport is 360 px high or less, else 32
grid.world: every instance outside the HUD starts on a whole UNIT, and a shape covers whole cells
grid.hud: held against the viewport's edges by anchor(), MARGIN inside them, and to the screen's edges by the Anchor behavior of anchored()

rules.says: A drawn image holds three alpha values: 0, 255 and the shadow's. A clear pixel is (0, 0, 0, 0), with no colour hidden under it to bleed into the edge when the image is scaled.
A shape is whole UNITs wide and high; its shadow hangs outside those cells.
An instance of a world layer starts on the grid: a shape is placed by the grid cell of its top-left corner.
An object created at runtime starts on the grid: its position is a random whole number of UNITs, never a raw random().
Every pixel that shows is a colour of PALETTE, named by the role it plays.
A label reads 4.5:1 against what is behind it, a title 3:1 (WCAG 2.2, 1.4.3).
A viewport 360 px high or less samples Nearest at a whole-number scale.

The project fills the screen at any aspect ratio: Scale outer, and Integer scale outer for pixel art, never a Letterbox mode with bars. A HUD element held to an edge carries the Anchor behavior for that edge; a backdrop or a dim reaches SCREEN_PAD past the viewport on every side.
rules.helpers: anchored(), hud_text(), hud_bar(), labelled_bar(), band_text(), screen_box(), backdrop(), anchor_types()

rules.says: Each layer lists its instances as an editor user would arrange them, back to front: the backdrop, the areas, then the rest by the Y of their feet; a child after its parent, a box inside another box after it unless the outer one is a label.

A value and its name are one group, GAP_IN apart; two groups, a HUD group and the playfield among them, sit at least 1.5 times the gap inside either apart, so a name stays with its value and not with the board.

The playfield's content is centred in what the HUD leaves, not on the whole screen, raised by OPTICAL_LIFT of that space's height; a centre more than a unit off prints a warning. The 5% lift is a rule of thumb with no measurement found behind it.
options: 0.05: the board a little above the middle of the play area, where the eye puts the middle
0: the board exactly in the middle of the play area

rules.says: The box around the playfield's content covers at least 15% of the screen, else the run prints a warning. Of the official 2D game examples' one-screen layouts, 95 in 100 cover more and the median covers 80%; the 25 to 60% band of slide and poster skills would flag 83% of them, so it is not used.

A check that the largest object is at least 1.5 times the area of the next: only 31% of the official 2D game examples' one-screen layouts pass it, since a grid of equal tiles, a deck of cards or two paddles is a sound game screen with no single largest object.
An ink outline inside a shape's edge where SHAPE_STYLE turns it on; off on the plain sheet, always on a hit frame.
No cast shadow on the plain sheet. A game that turns it on gets a hard one: one unblurred copy of the shape, one direction for the whole scene.
The shadow's offset, 2.7% of the viewport's shorter side.
The shadow at half opacity.
The shadow's direction, degrees clockwise from rightwards: down and to the right.
Two canvas greys, one solid grey, dim, ink and two accents, plus the hit's flash; the player in ink. The checker's greys at most 1.2:1, solid at least 3:1 on the darker of them.
rules.template: {role: '#%02X%02X%02X' % colour for role, colour in PALETTE.items()}

rules.says: An accent, a role that is a hue and not a grey, reads at least 3:1 on canvas_alt when drawn without an outline, or is drawn with its ink outline; every outlined fill reads at least 3:1 against the ink.
rules.template: [role for role in PALETTE if accent(role)]

rules.says: One Tiled Background behind everything, over the layout and SCREEN_PAD past it on every side, and no area elsewhere: the plain sheet in canvas, or, in a game with something transparent, a mask or a background still to come, the transparency checker, cells of UNIT / 2 in canvas and canvas_alt, the ruler in place of a grid.

Objects stay flat; an area or an edge is a Tiled Background of a pattern: low stripes for a harmless special surface, caution stripes for what moves or triggers, hazard stripes for what hurts. Stripes at 45 degrees, a one-unit tile, offset so pieces meet without a seam; the caution and hazard stripes cover strips and small zones, their shorter side a quarter of the viewport's at most.
rules.template: {kind: roles for kind, roles in PATTERNS.items() if kind not in BACKDROPS}

rules.says: A squash sets a share of the image's size at once, holds it, and tweens back to the image's size: a hit 0.8 x 1.2, back in 0.25 s easeoutback; a landing 1.2 x 0.8, back in 0.5 s easeoutelastic; a jump 0.7 x 1.3, held 0.2 s, back in 0.75 s easeoutelastic. A new squash stops the one running. hit() gives the hit's with the flash.
rules.template: [(k['width'], k['height'], k['hold'], k['seconds'], k['ease']) for k in SQUASH.values()]

rules.says: A squash acts on the drawn art, never on an object whose behavior collides: the art is a second object with its origin at its feet, pinned to an invisible collision mask.
A hit shows the shape's hit frame, filled in the flash role inside the ink outline with the same shadow, for 0.08 s of real time, then frame 0; never the Flash behavior.

A sprite is art(): its picture when it is in art/, else its stand-in, in the same box of whole units with the same origin and collision polygon. When the session has an image tool, the pictures come from it, prompted by prepare_art.py --list from ART_STYLE and each subject, then cut out and fitted by prepare_art.py. Art is not drawn in code.
Screen shake, size impact, slow motion at time scale 0.1 to 0.2, zoom impact; shake magnitudes in tiers of the viewport's shorter side.
Camera regions as level data: zoom, zoom speed, X/Y locks, X/Y offsets, target, local game speed.

BEATS gives each camera zone, or each round, wave or window of a one-screen game, a type and an intensity from 0 to 3. The first beat at 0; a beat of 2 or more followed by a rest that holds a pickup or a checkpoint, the climax by a rest or the exit; a mechanic taught alone before a beat combines it; one climax, in the last third; the last third more intense than the first. The generator prints the curve, one line a beat.

Every gap and step up of a level is measured against the player's reach from the Platform properties: easy up to half of it, hard from eight tenths, and the run stops past nine tenths. The reach is an approximation not yet measured in a preview.
Five short levels a world, an ordinary victory in about 1 to 2 s, a world's in 4 to 6 s, failure restarting within about 1 s.
A blurred translucent cast shadow reads as a smear on the checker.
Lighter parallax layers for depth.
Characters, finished art, fonts, exact palettes and third-party effects of any existing game.

deliver: Copy assets/build_project.py to the project's tools/ and rewrite only the game, above the helpers' begin marker and below their end marker: PROJECT_NAME, PALETTE's values by role, ART_STYLE, BEATS, build_images(), build_object_types(), build_layouts(), the module_*() functions.

Keep SHAPE_STYLE and the helpers between the markers; a helper the game changes is defined again below the end marker. Give every sprite an art() in whole units, which draws its stand-in until its picture arrives, and place it with shape_inst() on a grid cell; create runtime objects at grid_random().

With an image tool in the session: run prepare_art.py --list, make each picture with the prompt it prints, run prepare_art.py, then the generator. Never draw the art in code: it looks worse than the stand-ins and mixes styles.

Keep PALETTE's roles: a rectangle for the player, in ink, and for structure, in solid; a circle for what is collected, a triangle for what hurts. An area or an edge is area() of a pattern(); the backdrop is backdrop() of the plain pattern, or of the checker where something is transparent, a mask or a background still to come.

Place the HUD with hud_text(), hud_stat() for a value under its name, hud_bar(), labelled_bar() or band_text(), which hold it to the screen's edges with the Anchor behavior, and the playfield at centred(w, h, play_area(hud)); pass the HUD's groups and the playfield to spaced(). An instance placed by anchor() or row() takes behaviors=anchored(where). Lay a popup's dim over screen_box(), on the popup's own layer. Leave FULLSCREEN and z_order() as they are: they fill the screen and order each layer for any game.
Write BEATS for the game's zones or rounds, and read the curve the generator prints; measure every gap of a platformer level with jump().
Give every object that can be hit a hit_frame() after its shape and the Tween behavior, and show a hit with hit(obj), last in its block; never the Flash behavior.
Squash a landing and a jump with squash(art, "land") and squash(art, "jump"), on the art pinned to the collision mask, never on the mask.
Pass painted=True only for a picture meant to hold its own colours and soft edges.
Do not decide a rule whose status is open; ask the user, or keep the template's value.
confirm: python tools/build_project.py: the last line starts with ok:
python <skill>/scripts/check_look.py --project <folder>: the last line starts with ok:
python <skill>/scripts/prepare_art.py --list --project <folder>, where the art is meant to come from an image tool: no picture left to make
The look itself is the user's call on a screenshot; no script scores it.
